title: Structured Output Contract
summary: Design portable output contracts and independently validate parsing, size, shape, meaning, evidence, and authority before downstream use.
prerequisites: A framed task and a consumer that needs predictable output
Permission to create a local virtual environment and install the pinned dependency

sections.title: Separate shape from truth
paragraphs: Define the portable business contract first: fields, types, allowed values, evidence requirements, unknown handling, and version. Then map that contract to any provider-specific schema or tool mechanism in a separate adapter.

JSON objects map string keys to values. The required keyword identifies mandatory properties, while additionalProperties set to false rejects properties that are not declared by properties or matched by patternProperties. These structural rules do not establish factual accuracy, evidence quality, policy compliance, or authority. Source: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/object, retrieved 2026-09-19.

The fictional task in this lab classifies workshop registrations using only the supplied policy and records. The local program treats every candidate envelope as untrusted input. No model field, including nextAction, grants authority to the model, caller, or application.
sections.callout: Parseable is not the same as structurally valid, factually supported, authorized, or safe.

sections.title: Define a portable envelope
paragraphs: The envelope preserves the fields contractVersion, status, result, evidence, assumptions, warnings, and nextAction. It requires contractVersion 1.0, restricts status to complete, needs-input, or blocked, and closes both the envelope and each evidence object against unexpected properties.

The schema is shown in full for inspection and is embedded unchanged in the executable. Draft202012Validator.check_schema checks the schema against its meta-schema. Draft202012Validator.iter_errors yields validation errors for candidate instances. Source: https://python-jsonschema.readthedocs.io/en/stable/validate/, retrieved 2026-09-19.
The fictional policy and records are authoritative only inside this exercise. They say nothing about real people, workshops, registrations, providers, or permissions.
sections.callout: Use explicit needs-input or blocked states instead of forcing an unsupported answer.

sections.title: Distinguish historical status from registration permission
paragraphs: A historical registered record remains registered even if registrationOpen is false. Closing registration prevents or changes a new-registration path; it does not rewrite an existing historical record.

The declared rule is: registered maps to complete and waitlisted maps to needs-input. For an absent record, registrationOpen true maps to needs-input because a registration form may be offered, while registrationOpen false maps to blocked. The allowedTransitions policy explicitly contains these mappings.

The expected nextAction is independently selected from caller-owned policy. Matching a permitted action string does not itself perform the action. A model-generated nextAction never grants authority, and the lab performs no side effects.
sections.callout: Historical facts and permission for a new action are different policy inputs.

sections.title: Run the complete single-file validation lab
paragraphs: Save the following complete program as lab.py. Its embedded script metadata and runtime dependency check pin jsonschema to 4.26.0. The setup also installs exactly that version.

Python's standard json decoder does not apply JSON Schema. By default it accepts NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, and repeated object names. parse_constant can reject those non-standard constants. object_pairs_hook receives one ordered list of pairs for each decoded object, including nested objects. The unique_object hook processes the one list it receives and raises when that object contains a duplicate key. The decoder invokes the hook separately as it traverses nested objects. Source: https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html, retrieved 2026-09-19.

The validation pipeline checks input size, strict JSON parsing, schema shape, meaning, evidence, and caller-owned action policy in that order. It catches only expected input exceptions. Schema defects, programming errors, failed assertions, and unexpected exceptions remain visible.
sections.callout: The standard-library JSON parser and JSON Schema validator perform different jobs. Use both, followed by domain and authorization checks.

code.label: Complete executable program: lab.py

sections.title: Expected result and executable verification
paragraphs: The program asserts the expected result of every fixture before printing it. A regression raises AssertionError and stops execution rather than merely printing an unexpected result.

Stable codes are used instead of third-party ValidationError.message text, whose wording is not part of this lab's output contract. The exact stdout below is the expected fixture for the supplied program with Python 3.12 or later and jsonschema 4.26.0. It is not claimed as an observed run in the pinned environment or as provider or model execution.

The three positive envelope fixtures cover complete, needs-input, and blocked. Negative fixtures cover input size, malformed JSON, top-level and nested duplicate keys, explicit NaN, Infinity, and -Infinity, a pure type violation, extra properties, missing evidence, excessive field length, unsupported meaning, fabricated evidence, unsupported context, and unauthorized nextAction.
sections.callout: A passing schema check is one gate. It does not replace meaning, evidence, or authorization checks.

sections.title: Failure recovery
paragraphs: For a size or parse failure, discard the candidate and request a new JSON document. Do not silently repair malformed or ambiguous JSON because repair can change meaning. Duplicate keys and non-standard numeric constants must be rejected before schema validation.

For a shape failure, identify the stable failure category and ask for a new candidate that follows the contract. For a meaning or evidence failure, compare the candidate with trusted policy and records. A source string inside model output is only a provenance claim, not proof that the source exists or supports the claim.

For an authority failure, do not execute nextAction. Only trusted caller-owned code can decide whether a later side effect is permitted. The lab intentionally contains no network calls, API calls, external lookups, messages, registration changes, or other side effects.

If setup fails, confirm Python is version 3.12 or later, run python3 -m ensurepip --version, activate the new virtual environment, and reinstall from requirements.txt. If the protected lab path already exists, inspect or rename it rather than deleting or overwriting it automatically.
sections.callout: Never turn a parse, validation, evidence, or authorization error into permission.

sections.title: Learner task: apply a changed policy
paragraphs: Use the complete initial and modified inputs below. W-303 starts closed and changes to open. P-003 remains absent from W-303 in both record sets. Create one valid envelope for the initial input and a different valid envelope for the modified input.

Do not copy an answer from model output or treat nextAction as permission. Derive status and result from allowedTransitions, registrationOpen, and the historical record. Derive evidence only from records-v1, then compare nextAction with the caller-owned action policy implemented by the validator.

Run lab.py. Its variation-closed, variation-open, and variation-changed-outcome assertions provide executable verification that the full policy change produces a different outcome. Also confirm that extra-key, fabricated-source, and unauthorized-nextAction remain rejected.
sections.callout: The task gives the inputs and rules, not the completed envelopes. Produce both envelopes before opening the answer key.

code.label: Full initial and modified learner inputs

sections.title: Learner answer key and feedback
paragraphs: Initial answer: P-003 has no W-303 record and registration is closed, so the absent.closed transition produces blocked. The evidence states only the historical absence. Human review is the caller-owned permitted action text, not authority granted by the candidate.

Modified answer: the historical record is still absent, but registration is now open. The absent.open transition therefore produces needs-input, and the result reports that a registration path is open. The change from blocked to needs-input demonstrates a genuine policy-driven outcome change.

Feedback check: if both envelopes have the same status, the policy branch was not applied. If either says registered, the historical record was invented. If nextAction contains a different command, AUTH_NEXT_ACTION must reject it. Passing output never means that an action was executed.
sections.callout: registrationOpen controls the new-registration path. It does not create or erase a historical registered record.

code.label: Answer key: complete envelopes

sections.title: Adapt a local or hosted model portably
paragraphs: A local or hosted model may be asked to produce an envelope as candidate text. Keep provider request syntax in an adapter and pass returned text through the same size, strict parsing, shape, meaning, evidence, and authority gates.

Do not infer provider support, live execution, a real registration, source access, permission, or a completed side effect from a model response. The reusable business contract remains independent of any provider feature.

If an application later performs an action, authorization must come from trusted caller-owned identity, policy, and state checks outside the model response. The candidate may suggest text, but it cannot authorize itself.
sections.callout: Portable means independently validated at the contract boundary, not universally supported by every provider.

# The model response has no authority.
